top_signals.title: Odd Lots: What’s Behind the Classic Jackson Hole Photo Op?
top_signals.summary: For years, the Fed chair would give an address in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, and Wall Street and news organizations wouldn't have a recent photo of the chair to accompany stories. In steps Bloomberg's own Mike McKee. Tracy Alloway, Joe Weisenthal and Tom Keene learn the origin of the now traditional "Fed perp walk." (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Waterborne shipments from the U.S. Gulf Coast increased in April and May
top_signals.summary: Waterborne shipments of crude oil and petroleum products from the U.S. Gulf Coast (PADD 3) to the West Coast (PADD 5) more than quadrupled year-on-year in April and May following a waiver that permitted a broader group of ships to travel between U.S. ports. Shipments from the U.S. Gulf Coast to the East Coast (PADD 1) also increased.

top_signals.title: Por qué EE.UU. está detrás de una parte del petróleo de Venezuela
top_signals.summary: Aunque Venezuela ya no es la gran potencia petrolera que fue en el pasado, el país cuenta con algunas de las mayores reservas de petróleo del mundo. Desde que Estados Unidos destituyó al entonces presidente venezolano Nicolás Maduro el 3 de enero, ha restablecido las relaciones diplomáticas y está colaborando con el gobierno de la presidenta interina Delcy Rodríguez en Caracas. Pero esa relación está sujeta a numerosas condiciones: el presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, ha calificado a Vene

alerts.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
alerts.summary: A 26-year-old Canadian man once described as one of the most consequential cybercrime threat actors of 2024 has pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy to hack and extort more than 165 organizations that used the cloud data storage provider Snowflake. Connor Riley Moucka, of Kitchener, Ontario, also admitted to stealing call and text history records of more than 100 million AT&T customers.
